hook_text: Cover it, the number climbs. Warm it, the number drops. Sensors are just resistors that change.
clip_script: Meter on ohms. Clip the LDR. Covered by a hand: 800 kilohms. Uncovered: 3 kilohms. Torch: 300 ohms. More light, less resistance. Clip the thermistor. Bench: 10 kilohms. Warm fingers: 3 kilohms. That is NTC; a PTC goes the other way and makes a self-resetting fuse. Touch and moisture: two contacts and a gap; a finger or wet soil bridges it with a trickle. None of these can light an LED alone. They feed a transistor's base through a divider. Pick the one whose number swings most at the thing you want to catch. Test probes in the real water. Keep the LDR away from your own LED.
visual_style: Whiteboard multimeter with readings dropping as a hand lifts; thermistor between fingers with the number falling; two probes in soil with a trickle arrow; a chooser table: dark, hot, hand, wet.
pacing: Meter, LDR three readings, thermistor two readings, PTC, probes, divider, choose.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and record three LDR readings: dark, room, torch.
